numinance.kinds.v1.AutonomyFloor.jsonsch.description:
AutonomyFloor caps the level of the changes it matches; when floors from the org and control packs match, the
 lowest max_level holds.

match.description: match is required; the loader enforces it, the schema cannot.

max_level.description: max_level is required: no rule, default or narrower scope resolves a matching change above it.
max_level.title: Autonomy Level

numinance.kinds.v1.AutonomyFloor.jsonsch.title: Autonomy Floor

numinance.kinds.v1.AutonomyFloors.jsonsc.description: AutonomyFloors is the set of floors; it is one message so the whole set carries the FORBID directive.

rules.description: rules is required and non-empty; the loader enforces it, the schema cannot.

numinance.kinds.v1.AutonomyFloors.jsonsc.title: Autonomy Floors

numinance.kinds.v1.AutonomyMatch.jsonsch.description:
AutonomyMatch selects changes; an absent key matches every value and an empty match matches every change. In a
 rule, risk matches exactly and a key the change has no value for does not match. In a floor, risk matches that
 class and every higher one, and a key the change has no value for counts as a match.

environment.description: environment is the name of the environment the change acts in.

playbook.description: playbook is the name of the change's playbook.

risk.description: risk is the change's risk class, fixed at Classified.
risk.title: Risk Class

numinance.kinds.v1.AutonomyMatch.jsonsch.title: Autonomy Match

numinance.kinds.v1.Control.jsonschema.st.description: Control is one requirement of the framework.

approval.description: approval is the human approval the control requires; absent requires none beyond the stage gates.

id.description: id is required: the control's id within the pack, such as "req-6.4.2".

requires_evidence.description:
requires_evidence names the evidence a change the control applies to must record, unique; missing declared evidence
 turns success into PARTIAL.

numinance.kinds.v1.Control.jsonschema.st.title: Control

numinance.kinds.v1.ControlApproval.jsons.description:
ControlApproval is the approval a control requires. Policy enforces it at the release gate (and the plan gate where a
 stage declares one) whatever the StageRegistry contains; it only adds to the registry's gates. The loader refuses group
 or dual_control unless human is true.

dual_control.description:
dual_control is true when two distinct human principals, neither the author nor acting in the author's run, must
 approve; absent means false.

group.description:
group names the approver group the approver must belong to; membership comes from the org's identity provider,
 never from repository files.

human.description: human is true when a human principal must approve; absent means false.

numinance.kinds.v1.ControlApproval.jsons.title: Control Approval

numinance.kinds.v1.ControlFloors.jsonsch.description: ControlFloors is the set of floors a pack adds; it is one message so the whole set carries the FORBID directive.

autonomy.description: autonomy caps levels as AutonomyPolicy floors do; the lowest matching max_level of the org and every pack holds.

residency.description: residency adds residency floors as ResidencyPolicy floors do; every floor of the org and every pack holds.

numinance.kinds.v1.ControlFloors.jsonsch.title: Control Floors

numinance.kinds.v1.ControlPackSpec.jsons.description: ControlPackSpec says which framework the pack reads, when it applies, and what it requires.

applicability.description:
applicability is a CEL expression over policy-computed facts of the change that selects the changes the pack's
 controls and floors apply to; absent means every change of a component whose resolved profile names the pack. One
 line of at most 4096 bytes; the profile context compiles it to a bool, and an evaluation error means the pack applies.

controls.description: controls is required, non-empty and unique by id.

effective_date.description: effective_date is required: the day the framework version takes effect, as YYYY-MM-DD.

export_views.description: export_views are the evidence export views the pack offers, unique by name.

floors.description: floors are the floors the pack adds; they combine with the org's floors (or the shipped ones) and only tighten.

framework.description: framework is required: the framework's name, such as "pci-dss".

jurisdiction.description: jurisdiction is required: where the framework applies, such as "global" or "eu".

sources.description: sources cite the texts the pack reads, unique; each is one line of at most 1024 bytes.

version.description: version is required: the framework's version, such as "4.0.1".

numinance.kinds.v1.ControlPackSpec.jsons.title: Control Pack Spec

numinance.kinds.v1.ExportView.jsonschema.description: ExportView is a named selection of a change's evidence for one audience, such as one requirement of the framework.

controls.description: controls is required and non-empty: the ids of the pack's controls whose evidence the view exports, unique.

name.description: name is required: the view's name, as numi evidence export --view takes it.

numinance.kinds.v1.ExportView.jsonschema.title: Export View

numinance.kinds.v1.ResidencyFloors.jsons.description: ResidencyFloors is the set of floors; it is one message so the whole set carries the FORBID directive.

floor.description: floor is required: it applies to every change, together with every matching rule's floor.
floor.title: Residency Class

rules.description: rules add floors per component and environment; a rule never relaxes floor.

numinance.kinds.v1.ResidencyFloors.jsons.title: Residency Floors

numinance.kinds.v1.ResidencyMatch.jsonsc.description:
ResidencyMatch selects changes; an absent key matches every value and an empty match matches every change, and a
 key the change has no value for counts as a match. Floors from the org and control packs all hold together.

component.description:
component is the name of the component the change touches. It is not a security boundary until floors match only
 components of an org-owned SIGNED_POLICY registry, since a repo can rename one.

environment.description: environment is the name of the environment the change acts in.

numinance.kinds.v1.ResidencyMatch.jsonsc.title: Residency Match

numinance.kinds.v1.ResidencyRule.jsonsch.description: ResidencyRule adds a floor for the changes it matches.

match.description: match is required; the loader enforces it, the schema cannot.

numinance.kinds.v1.ResidencyRule.jsonsch.title: Residency Rule
